title: Drifting Apart
subject: geology
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten entries on a surface that will not hold still.

entries.clue: Fracture with movement on either side, or the blame
Stationary plume beneath a travelling plate
Dark rock that floors most of the oceans
___ spreading, the ridge-driven half of the theory
One plate going down beneath another
Range raised by the Nazca plate's slow dive
Alfred who argued in 1912 that the continents had moved
Deep sea furrow marking where crust descends
Supercontinent that came apart in the Mesozoic

factCards.text: Alfred Wegener set out his case for continental drift from 1912, but it was only accepted after seafloor spreading and magnetic striping were mapped in the 1960s.
factCards.sourceTitle: Wegener, Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane (1915)

factCards.text: Oceanic crust is denser than continental crust, which is why the ocean floor is the side that descends where the two meet.
factCards.sourceTitle: US Geological Survey, This Dynamic Earth

factCards.text: The Hawaiian island chain records a plate travelling over a fixed hotspot: the islands grow older with distance from the active volcanoes.
factCards.sourceTitle: US Geological Survey, Hawaiian Volcano Observatory
